title: Emergency physician
description: The whole curriculum again + detailed medicine knowledge, dose calculation, skin and breathing signs.

questions.q: 70 kg patient, Fentanyl 1 mcg/kg. What is the dose?
answers: 70 mcg
7 mcg
700 mcg
0.7 mg

questions.q: 90 kg patient, Rocuronium 1.2 mg/kg. How much?
answers: 108 mg
120 mg
90 mg

questions.q: 60 kg patient, Midazolam 0.05 mg/kg. How much?
answers: 3 mg
30 mg
0.3 mg
6 mg

questions.q: 80 kg patient, Insulin 0.1 IU/kg. How much?
answers: 8 IU
80 IU
0.8 IU
10 IU

questions.q: What is the risk of the 2 mg/kg (orange) Ketamine dose?
answers: A stronger effect than usual: only when there is a reason
A weaker effect than usual: the patient may wake up early
None: Ketamine has no upper limit, it keeps the breathing
It is the child dose: in an adult it is too low to work

questions.q: Midazolam 0.1 mg/kg for a drunk patient. What do you expect?
answers: More depressed breathing: be ready to secure the airway
A weaker effect, because alcohol speeds up its breakdown
Agitation: alcohol turns Midazolam into a stimulant
No change: Naloxone reverses it if the breathing slows

questions.q: Fentanyl and Midazolam together. What happens?
answers: Their effects add up: depressed breathing and circulation
They weaken each other, so both doses must be increased
Only the pain relief adds up, the breathing is unchanged
Midazolam blocks the Fentanyl effect on the breathing

questions.q: When do you give Insulin prehospitally?
answers: Rarely: only for a confirmed, very high blood glucose, with repeated measurements
To every diabetic patient who forgot their own dose today, to be safe
To every unconscious diabetic, even before the glucose is measured
Always together with Glucose 40%, so the glucose does not swing

questions.q: Very high blood glucose, dehydrated patient. What is the basis of prehospital care?
answers: IV fluids, which slowly lower the blood glucose too
A large Insulin bolus IV, fluids only in the hospital
Only small sips of water, IV fluid makes it worse
Insulin under the skin and keeping fluids restricted

questions.q: Head injury with high blood pressure and a slow pulse. What does it mean?
answers: Raised pressure in the skull (Cushing reflex): urgent transport
Pain reaction after the trauma: give pain relief and watch
Spinal shock from a neck injury: fluids and lying flat
Hidden bleeding in the abdomen: fluids and raise the legs

questions.q: Unequal pupils, clear fluid from the ear?
answers: Severe head injury, suspected skull base fracture
Stroke with a bleed, after a fall from standing
Ear infection with pressure on one eye nerve
Concussion, the fluid is from the outer ear wound

questions.q: Cold, sweaty skin. What do you think of first?
answers: Hypoglycaemia or stimulant poisoning
Very high blood glucose or dehydration
Opioid or sleeping pill poisoning
Fever with an infection or heatstroke

questions.q: Dry skin, a lot of urine, very high blood glucose. What is behind it?
answers: Dehydration from the high blood glucose
Kidney failure, so fluids must be limited
Too much fluid intake, the body drains it
Overdose of the patient's own Insulin

questions.q: Bitten tongue, wet trousers, confusion that clears by itself?
answers: The state after a seizure (postictal)
A stroke that is getting better (TIA)
Hypoglycaemia that corrected itself
Alcohol poisoning wearing off slowly

questions.q: Why does Naloxone not help in a sleeping pill overdose?
answers: Because it only reverses opioids
Because it is too weak for that dose
Because it only works through the IV
It does help, it is the antidote

questions.q: Low blood pressure around an arrest (systolic 60). What do you give?
answers: Push-dose Adrenaline (0.02 mg) and look for the cause
A 1 mg Adrenaline bolus IV, as in cardiac arrest
Nitroglycerin spray to improve the heart's blood flow
Nothing: wait for the pulse to stop, then start CPR

questions.q: Nitroglycerin when the patient took a potency pill (PDE5 inhibitor)?
answers: Contraindicated: severe drop in blood pressure
Allowed, but only half of the usual dose
Allowed if the pill was taken over 2 hours ago
Safe: the two medicines do not interact

questions.q: Pulmonary oedema, blood pressure 210/120. What is the treatment?
answers: Nitroglycerin, oxygen, sit up
Fluid bolus, oxygen, lie flat
Salbutamol, oxygen, sit up
Captopril only, then lie flat

questions.q: Hypoglycaemic, awake and able to swallow. What is the simplest?
answers: Glucose gel
Glucose 40% IV
IV fluid only
Wait and remeasure

questions.q: What can an unsynchronised shock cause in VT with a pulse?
answers: Ventricular fibrillation
A burn, but nothing more
Asystole in every case
It is safe and preferred

questions.q: Why must Adrenaline be repeated every 3–5 minutes during CPR?
answers: Because its effect is short, a few minutes
Because the first dose is only a test dose
Because each dose must be higher than the last
Because it is absorbed slowly during CPR

questions.q: Stroke patient, systolic 110. What is the problem?
answers: Below 130 less blood reaches the brain and it gets worse faster
Nothing: it is an ideal value that protects against a brain bleed
It is still too high: it must go below 100 with Captopril
It only matters above 220, everything below is acceptable

questions.q: Fluid loss of a burned patient?
answers: Plasma loss: the dressing reduces it, early transport
Only sweating: drink water, no hurry with transport
Blood loss: a pressure bandage on the burns stops it
Plasma loss: open the blisters to drain the fluid

questions.q: Open fracture with critical bleeding. What is the order?
answers: First stop the bleeding with a bandage, then the splint
First the splint, the bleeding stops when it is still
First push the bone back in, then bandage and splint
First pain relief and IV, then bandage and splint

questions.q: A hypoglycaemic patient woke up after glucose. What do you watch?
answers: Measure the glucose again, it can fall again
Give Insulin so the glucose does not go too high
Nothing: once awake, the glucose stays normal
Only the breathing, the glucose cannot change

questions.q: What do you expect with an extremely high blood glucose (above 700 mg/dL)?
answers: Confusion, even unconsciousness
Cold sweat, shaking, fast pulse
A patient without any signs
Pinpoint pupils, slow breathing

questions.q: Asthma, silent chest, exhausted, SpO2 74%. What do you do?
answers: Salbutamol, oxygen; if it gets worse, consider RSI
Midazolam to calm the breathing, then oxygen
Oxygen only; the silent chest means it improved
Nitroglycerin and oxygen, sit the patient up

questions.q: Which belong to the “4T” reversible causes of cardiac arrest?
answers: Tension pneumothorax, tamponade, toxins, thrombosis
Tension pneumothorax, trauma, temperature, tachycardia
Tamponade, toxins, thrombosis, hypothermia
Trauma, tamponade, tachycardia, toxins
